newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sees boom in future electricity use.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees boom in future electricity use.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Ministry said in a recently released report the country's demand for electricity is likely to boom in the next several years.

A ministry report on national electricity use said the country would consume 143,604 gigawatt-hours of electricity in 2000 and 185,699 gigawatt-hours in 2005 -- a 25-percent and 61-percent rise respectively from current levels.
Electricity use is expected to grow in all regions of the nation, and especially in the highly populated central zone.

To supply the expected increased electricity demand, the government estimated it would need to add 12.76 gigawatts of capacity to the national electric system between 1996 and 2005, of which 9.77 gigawatts would come from new projects, the ministry said.
Natural gas needed to supply the higher electricity generation should total 2.414 billion cubic feet per day (cfd) in 2005, compared with 506 million cfd in 1995.

"The projects either planned or in construction represent the efforts of the federal government and the private sector to strengthen the diversification of sources of energy," the report, released on Thursday, said.
Mexico's electricity expansion projects allow private capital in 26 projects.

Private energy consumption reached 9.6 gigawatt-hours in 1996, or 8.3 percent of the total use. For the next decade, private consumption is expected to rise six percent per year to 9.2 percent of total national electricity use by 2005, the report said.
Sixteen new generators slated for operation by 2000 should yield a total capacity of 2.996 megawatts, the report said.
Investment needed for the electricity sector from 1996 to 2005 will total 187.481 billion pesos, the ministry study said.
Mexico's electricity generating capacity has 69,868 km of transmission lines, the report said.
